answer.evidence: The tarp roof fills rows 0-13 as a large sloped plane with mottled green texture. A light front-edge line sits at row 13, followed by dark eave shadow at rows 14-15, and the width narrows to 32 at row 16 where the stall opens. Below it the crate counter has a tan top strip at rows 17-22 with goods on it (decor), then a plank front face with dark bands at rows 23-31, about 16 rows of front face in total. The roof top surface and the front face both read clearly, so it is a 3/4 view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The closest reference is the cheese stall, and the candidate falls short of it on tone count. The candidate shows 11 visible tones per tile against 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the roofed well. It has 22 distinct colours overall against 40 and 38. It is only level with the hedge, which is a much simpler prop. Strengths: the dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines lean green or brown and read as dark material tone. Near-flat coverage is 0%, and the tarp has ridge and fold texture with a few lighter highlights. Weaknesses: the tarp ramp is about 4 greens, not the 5-6 steps Beodeul uses. The crate counter is dark and compact, and its scrap parts, cloth and can are tiny and lightly shaded, so they are less detailed than the cheese stall's goods and awning stripes. Overall it is clean and has no sticker outline, but it is thinner than the same-kind reference, and with this much doubt it fails.
